::: {.callout-important}
## Not part of the governance engine
The AAN book series and this training program are **companion material for
the federal vertical — they are not part of the governance engine**. The reference implementation's core is
vertical-agnostic; the AAN corpus is external federal-modernization content that the reference implementation's
conformance tooling happens to consume as evidence. Nothing on these pages
is host-repo canon, defines engine doctrine, or is scoped for a `UIAO_NNN`
allocation. These pages are hosted here for convenience alongside the
adapter that binds the books' evidence.
:::

::: {.callout-note}
## Living program — expansion expected
This program is a **research-driven living curriculum**. It launches with the
program charter, the two track outlines, and a first-pass vendor training
catalog. As research continues, modules gain per-book lesson pages, labs,
assessment rubrics, and additional vendor offerings. See
[Expansion roadmap](#expansion-roadmap).
:::

## What this program is

The Federal Application-Aware Networking (AAN) series spans nine volumes;
this training program covers its **20 core books** (Book 00 through Book 19)
that document a complete federal network modernization: landing zone and IPAM, network access control, cryptographic
identity, the HR-driven identity and organizational SSOT, network and
telecommunications modernization, data-platform authentication, privileged access, vulnerability
management, data protection, detection engineering, business continuity,
supply-chain risk, program governance, PII transparency, cybersecurity
training, and the authorization package / ConMon wrapper. The books live in
draft staging at
[`docs/customer-documents/federal-aan-series/`](https://github.com/WhalerMike/uiao/tree/main/inbox/Application%20Aware%20Networking)
and are bound to FedRAMP 20x evidence slots by the
[`fedramp_aan_catalog` adapter](https://github.com/WhalerMike/uiao/tree/main/src/uiao/adapters/fedramp_aan_catalog).

![Figure 1 — The program at a glance: 20 books produce artifacts, eight slot mappings bind them as evidence, and two tracks teach the corpus.](figs/tp-fig-01-program-map.png){fig-alt="AAN Training Program map: twenty books feed eight evidence slots, taught by two tracks"}

The AAN Training Program teaches that corpus in **two tracks**:

| Track | Page | Audience | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Track A — Compliance** | [Compliance track](compliance-track.html) | ISSOs / ISSMs, assessors, ConMon operators, compliance leads | Can state, for each of the 20 books, which NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 controls it closes, which FedRAMP 20x KSI category evaluates that closure, and how the evidence flows through the engine's conformance pipeline |
| **Track B — Implementation** | [Implementation track](implementation-track.html) | Network, platform, database, identity, and security engineers | Can implement the architecture each book describes and produce the machine-readable evidence Track A consumes |

A third page, the [Vendor training catalog](vendor-training-catalog.html),
maps each book to existing external training from the vendors whose products
the books deploy (Microsoft, Infoblox, Cisco, AWS, and others), plus
federal/compliance training sources (CISA, FedRAMP, NIST).

## Relationship to governance engines

- This program is **separate from** the reference implementation's own training program
  (Contributor + Operator tracks). That program teaches the reference implementation; this
  program teaches the **federal AAN book series**, which is not the governance engine
  material. The only connection is mechanical: the
  `fedramp_aan_catalog` conformance adapter reads the books' artifacts as
  evidence, the same way the engine's adapters read any external vendor's output.
- The engine core is vertical-agnostic. Describing this curriculum as part of
  any governance engine would itself be a positioning bug.
- The compliance backbone follows the
  [Federal AAN / ConMon Compliance Gap Roadmap](https://github.com/WhalerMike/uiao/blob/main/inbox/Application%20Aware%20Networking/federal-aan-conmon-gap-roadmap.md)
  and the slot bindings in
  [`fedramp_aan_catalog/mappings/`](https://github.com/WhalerMike/uiao/tree/main/src/uiao/adapters/fedramp_aan_catalog/mappings).

::: {.callout-warning}
## Provenance status
The AAN books currently live under `inbox/` — the repo's **draft staging**
surface. They are external companion material, not host-repo canon, and are not
on a canonization path. If the books move to their own home, the links
below follow them. Treat control-closure counts as working figures from the
gap roadmap, not attested facts.
:::

## Program structure

1. **Orientation (both tracks)** — read Book 00 and the
   [gap roadmap](https://github.com/WhalerMike/uiao/blob/main/inbox/Application%20Aware%20Networking/federal-aan-conmon-gap-roadmap.md);
   understand the FedRAMP 20x timeline (Class A opens August 3, 2026; 20x
   mandatory January 2027; BOD 26-04 VDR/VER due December 7, 2026).
2. **Pick a track** — [Track A Compliance](compliance-track.html) or
   [Track B Implementation](implementation-track.html). The tracks share the
   corpus but read it differently: Track A reads books as *control-closure
   evidence*; Track B reads them as *build instructions*.
3. **Supplement with vendor training** — each module points into the
   [vendor training catalog](vendor-training-catalog.html) for the underlying
   product skills (Entra, Sentinel, Purview, Infoblox DDI, SD-WAN, …).
4. **Capstone (both tracks)** — produce or evaluate a KSI evidence bundle
   with the engine CLI (`<engine> ksi evaluate`, `<engine> oscal ksi-ar`,
   `<engine> oscal generate`) against the eight AAN evidence slots.

![Figure 2 — The evidence flow both capstones exercise: a book artifact is bound by a slot mapping, evaluated against KSI rules, and lands as per-KSI verdicts in the OSCAL Assessment Results.](figs/tp-fig-06-evidence-flow.png){fig-alt="Evidence flow: book artifact to slot mapping to KSI evaluation to OSCAL assessment results"}

## The Core AAN Pathway {#core-aan-pathway}

The full program walks all 20 books; most ISSOs and engineers should
**start with the nine-book spine** below, which feeds six of the eight
evidence slots directly and exercises both capstone surfaces:

| Book | Module page | Why it is in the spine | Slot(s) fed |
|---|---|---|---|
| 00 | [Executive Summary](books/book-00.html) | The argument and the deadline map | — (orientation) |
| 01 | [SSA Landing Zone, IPAM & FedRAMP](books/book-01.html) | Addressing is the dependency everything else assumes | 2 |
| 03 | [Certificates, Tokens & Cryptographic Identity](books/book-03.html) | The credential plane | 1 |
| 04 | [HRIT Identity & Org SSOT](books/book-04.html) | The lifecycle source of truth | 1 |
| 05 | [Network Modernization](books/book-05.html) | The application-aware transport argument | 3 |
| 10 | [Privileged Access Management](books/book-10.html) | The highest-blast-radius identity surface | 1, 5 |
| 11 | [Vulnerability Management](books/book-11.html) | The KEV-driven telemetry spine | 4, 5, 6 |
| 13 | [SIEM / XDR Detection](books/book-13.html) | Detection engineering closes the telemetry loop | 4, 6 |
| 19 | [Authorization Package & ConMon](books/book-19.html) | Assembles everything into the package | (assembles all) |

Pair the spine with the four scripted labs
([DDI](labs/lab-b1-ddi.html), [PIM](labs/lab-b5-pim.html),
[Sentinel](labs/lab-b6-sentinel.html), [Purview](labs/lab-b6-purview.html)).

The pathway is a **starting sequence, not a credential path**: slots 7
(continuity — Book 14) and 8 (training — Book 18), the supply-chain depth
of Book 15, and the full capstones still come from the complete tracks,
and the Track A pass bar remains all eight slots. Read the spine, run the
labs, then finish the track you belong to.

## The `<engine>` token — what the commands run {#tooling-stack}

Every command block in this program writes `<engine>` where a CLI name
would go. It is a **substitution token, not a product**: the program is
engine-neutral, and the commands are defined by the
[AAN Evidence & Authorization Contract](https://github.com/WhalerMike/uiao/blob/main/docs/customer-documents/federal-aan-series/AAN_Evidence_Contract_Spec.qmd)
— the open specification (compliance spine + eight evidence slots + OSCAL
AP/AR/POA&M boundary) that any conformant evidence engine can satisfy.
Substitute the CLI name of whichever conformant engine your agency runs.

The three commands the capstones need:

| Command | What it does | What you get |
|---|---|---|
| `<engine> ksi evaluate --ir <file> --out <file>` | Evaluates a machine-readable evidence (IR) file against the KSI rules | Per-rule verdicts (the raw scoring pass) |
| `<engine> oscal ksi-ar --output <file>` | Builds Assessment Results from the eight AAN slot evidence bindings | Per-KSI satisfied / not-satisfied / not-evaluated verdicts — the artifact both capstones require |
| `<engine> oscal generate` | Generates the OSCAL package documents from an evidence bundle | SSP / POA&M material for the Book 19 assembly |

**What Tier F actually runs:** the host repository that publishes these
pages ships a reference engine satisfying the contract, alongside the
[slot mapping files](https://github.com/WhalerMike/uiao/tree/main/src/uiao/adapters/fedramp_aan_catalog/mappings)
the curriculum is derived from. The fixture path is: clone the
repository, install the reference engine per its README, substitute its
CLI name for `<engine>`, and run the three commands above — no cloud
footprint required (see the [lab tiers](labs/index.html#lab-tiers)).

## Completion criteria

Borrowing the pattern of the reference implementation's training program (no parallel
certification system), without being part of that program:

- **Track A** — a clean walk of all eight slot mappings: for each slot, name
  the books that feed it, the KSI category that evaluates it, and produce a
  `<engine> oscal ksi-ar` run showing each KSI verdict (satisfied /
  not-satisfied / not-evaluated), with a short written gap statement for
  anything not yet evaluable.
- **Track B** — implement (or lab-simulate) one module end-to-end and land
  its evidence artifact where the slot mappings can bind it, verified by
  regenerating the KSI Assessment Results (`<engine> oscal ksi-ar`) and seeing
  the slot's verdict reflect the new evidence.

  ([B6](labs/lab-b6-sentinel.html)), and Purview
  ([B6](labs/lab-b6-purview.html)), tiered fixture / trial-tenant /

  eval-gear labs.
- ✅ **Assessment rubrics** — shipped:
  [per-slot scoring sheets](assessment-rubrics.html) for the Track A
  capstone with a four-level scale and explicit pass bar.
- ✅ **Corpus sync (July 2026)** — Books 18 (Training & Awareness) and 19
  (Authorization Package & ConMon) joined the corpus; slot 8 — training
  (KSI-CED) joined the evidence model, taking the series' internal 29-rule KSI decomposition to fully evaluable. Module pages, tracks, rubrics, and figures updated.
- ✅ **Series restructure sync (July 2026)** — resynced to the 20-book
  FedAAN series: three new early books (02 Network Access Control,
  03 Certificates/Tokens, 04 HRIT Identity & Org SSOT), all downstream
  books renumbered (+3), filenames moved to the `FedAAN_` scheme, module
  pages/tracks/figures/rubrics/bundle regenerated.
- ✅ **External-evaluation response (July 2026)** — the program was
  independently reviewed (see the evaluation and its graded assessment in
  the series directory); this wave shipped the graded response: the
  [Core AAN Pathway](#core-aan-pathway), the
  [`<engine>` tooling note](#tooling-stack), the PIM lab's
  bind-the-evidence close, boundary-context cross-links from Books
  05/06/11/12/13, the
  [post-implementation KPIs](assessment-rubrics.html#post-implementation-kpis),
  and stable Date Codes replacing render-time dates on every page.
- **A permanent home** — this material is not the governance engine's and will not be
  canonized as a `UIAO_NNN` spec; if the AAN corpus moves to its own
  repo/product, the program moves with it.
